questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a . This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually. b . The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually. c . While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so. d . It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

a. This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually.

b. The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually.

c. While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so.

d. It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas.

options.html: d, b, a, c
a, c, b, d
b, d, a, c
b, d, c, a

questions.solution: The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I will not be able to ___________ my assignment in time
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I will not be able to ___________ my assignment in time
questions.solution: complete' will be used because it is the base form of the verb, and in future tense sentences, 'will' is followed by the base form. The sentence indicates that the speaker will not be able to finish their assignment on time. Whereas, 'completes' is used in present tense for the third person singular (he, she, it). 'Completing' is the present participle used in continuous tenses, which does not fit here. 'Completed' is the past tense or past participle and is not suitable for this future tense sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As 'brutal' is synonymous to 'harsh', 'naive' is synonymous to ________.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As 'brutal' is synonymous to 'harsh', 'naive' is synonymous to ________.
questions.solution: 'Simple' will be used because 'naive' means innocent or straightforward, which is synonymous with 'simple'. The question discusses the synonym relationship between the given words. Whereas, 'worldly' means sophisticated or experienced, 'wise' means intelligent, and 'hospitable' means welcoming or generous, none of which fit in this context.

My cousin thinks that / English is difficult / than other subjects

options.html: My cousin thinks that

questions.solution: ‘more difficult than other subjects’ will be used instead of ‘difficult than other subjects’ because when comparing using adjectives that have two or more syllables (like difficult), the comparative form is made by adding ‘more’ before the adjective. So, to make a grammatically correct comparative sentence, it should be: English is more difficult than other subjects; Like— English is more difficult than Mathematics.

questions.solution: "Irreconcilable" means "impossible to reconcile or bring into agreement." In the sentence, it is implied that while the subjects may differ or seem very different, they are not "irreconcilable," suggesting that reconciliation or harmony is possible. questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. P. Whether it is scorching summers or bone-chilling winters, Q. In India, tea transcends mere consumption; it embodies a lifestyle R. Whether in the bustling streets of Mumbai or the serene backwaters of Kerala, the clinking of tea cups resonates, marking the essence of every region in the country S. tea is a remedy that brings Indians together to start the day, refuel, or simply enjoy a moment of solace
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

P. Whether it is scorching summers or bone-chilling winters,

Q. In India, tea transcends mere consumption; it embodies a lifestyle

R. Whether in the bustling streets of Mumbai or the serene backwaters of Kerala, the clinking of tea cups resonates, marking the essence of every region in the country

S. tea is a remedy that brings Indians together to start the day, refuel, or simply enjoy a moment of solace
questions.solution: Q sentence paragraph की शुरुआत करता है क्योंकि यह बताता है कि “In India, tea transcends mere consumption; it embodies a lifestyle” यानी भारत में चाय सिर्फ एक पेय नहीं है, यह एक lifestyle का हिस्सा है। यह पूरे paragraph का main idea सेट करता है और चाय की cultural significance को introduce करता है।
